findings.description: firstSentence's new lazy bold-title group makes the cut quadratic: a session-written agent line of `**` followed by about 1 MiB of `*` stalls every later worker launch and fix-round compile for minutes, where the old regex was linear.
PR rewrites the landed text of ADR 0183 in place. docs/adr/README.md says a later change appends a dated amendment section (with the PR) or adds a new decision that links back through `Amends:`.
findings.body:
Decision 183 is already on main: the merge base contains its commits 8698f31 through d3f87d5. This diff rewrites its checklist sentence in place. The landed text said "each cut to its first sentence". The new text says a bold-led paragraph "keeps its title and its body's first sentence" and adds a new rule that "a non-bold one is left out by design, whatever it says". That changes the decision, not just its wording.

`docs/adr/README.md` L19-21:

> An open PR may still edit the decision it adds. Once a decision has landed, a later change appends an amendment section to it (dated, with the PR) or adds a new decision that links back through `Amends:`. It does not rewrite the landed text.

This same file already follows that rule. Commit d3f87d5 ("keep 0183's landed respawn sentence, amend it as dated") left the landed text and appended `*The respawn (2026-11-14, #334).* This supersedes ...`. After this rewrite, a reader can no longer tell what #323 decided from what #346 changed.

**Fix.** Restore the landed sentence. Then append a dated amendment, in the style of the existing respawn one (for example `*The checklist cut (2026-11-16, #346).*`). It should say that a bold-led paragraph keeps its title plus its body's first sentence, and that a non-bold lead paragraph is left out by design.
